 "Hard to combine with EAGLE-style drafters, which need target features that a drafter running ahead does not have yet. Its int4 latency kernels do not suit high-throughput serving, and results cover single requests with 4-bit AWQ targets.",
 "async / multi-device")

add("logitspec",
 "Uses the last logit twice: besides the next token, its top-ranked entries often contain the token after it. Those candidates join the next token in a two-token query against prompt n-grams, which finds correct references more often than single-suffix retrieval. Training-free.",
 "It retrieves only from the prompt, so short prompts give little to copy, and by its own account its end-to-end speedup trails draft-model methods. Main results are greedy at batch size 1.",
 "retrieval drafting")

add("rhymerl",
 "Speeds RL rollouts by drafting from the same prompt's responses in earlier epochs (HistoSpec): suffix trees over past rollouts, built asynchronously, supply drafts, and an AIMD rule sets draft length. HistoPipe also uses past lengths to balance rollout workers.",
 "Drafts are verbatim copies of history, so they need the prompt to recur across epochs and help only where the policy still repeats itself. Sibling responses being generated in the same step contribute nothing.",
 "RL rollouts")

add("gto",
 "Trains the drafter on the quantity decoding uses: Draft Tree Reward, the expected acceptance length of the decoding-time draft tree under the target, computed without sampling and optimized with group-standardized advantages and a PPO-style surrogate along the longest accepted path.",
 "Needs substantial extra training compute (hundreds of A100 GPU-hours for 8B to 70B targets), and it was evaluated only at batch size 1 with trees at most 8 deep.",
 "drafter training")

add("diffuspec",
 "Uses a pretrained diffusion LM (Dream-7B) as a training-free drafter that proposes a whole block in one pass. A causal-consistency search picks a left-to-right path through the per-position candidates, scored by diffusion log-prob plus a 3-gram proxy, and draft length adapts each round.",
 "The 7B diffusion drafter is memory-heavy and lacks KV reuse and fused kernels, and the 3-gram proxy only weakly enforces left-to-right coherence. Evaluated only at greedy decoding, batch 1, with one 32B target.",
 "diffusion drafting")

add("respec",
 "Adapts EAGLE-3 to RL rollouts: an offline-profiled scheduler changes draft steps, branching and token counts, or turns SD off, as the active batch shrinks, while the drafter is continuously distilled from the changing actor with reward-weighted KD, overlapped with generation.",
 "Tested only on math GRPO with Qwen2.5 3B to 14B. Its claim that plain EAGLE-3 lowers RL reward conflicts with lossless verification and is left unexplained, which suggests its pipeline was not exactly lossless.",
 "RL rollouts")

add("c_2510_22876",
 "Shows that published batched-SD implementations silently change outputs, and states two invariants needed for equivalence with contiguous KV layouts: rectangular alignment and position-ID/KV contiguity. EqSpec enforces them without custom kernels; EXSpec batches same-length sequences to skip realignment.",
 "Covers only contiguous-KV setups, not the paged caches of vLLM or SGLang. Realignment overhead grows superlinearly with batch, limiting gains to moderate batch, and exact match reaches only 90.8-97.3% because of floating-point nondeterminism.",
 "batched SD correctness")

add("tlt",
 "Keeps a drafter current during RL by retraining a one-layer EAGLE drafter on GPUs idled by long-tail rollouts. A bandit picks draft depth and verify width from the running-request count over pre-captured CUDA graphs, with a model-free n-gram drafter for early steps.",
 "SD switches on only once fewer than about 32 requests remain, so the bulk of each rollout gets no speedup. The single-layer drafter is a compromise: EAGLE-3-style training was too costly to fit inside rollout bubbles.",
 "RL rollouts")

add("das",
 "Training-free drafting for RL rollouts: a per-problem suffix tree over a sliding window of recent rollouts tracks policy drift, and a latency-model budget gives long, straggling requests large draft budgets and turns speculation off for short ones.",
 "Each sample drafts only from past rollouts, so what its siblings are generating in the same step goes unused. Budgets rely on a heuristic 3-class length predictor, and results cover only 7-8B models.",
 "RL rollouts")

add("seer",
 "An RL rollout system whose grouped SD keeps one compressed suffix tree per prompt group, fed live by all in-flight samples of that prompt, so each sample drafts from its siblings' progress. Draft length adapts, alongside divided rollout and length-aware scheduling.",
 "Drafts are verbatim copies of sibling text with no learned drafter, so acceptance stays around 2-3 tokens and stops wherever siblings phrase things differently. Group context adds only about 0.22 tokens over a plain suffix tree.",
 "sibling drafting")

add("specdiff2",
 "Fine-tunes a 7B diffusion drafter with streak distillation, which maximizes a surrogate of the expected accepted streak on target-sampled paths. At decode time it samples K drafts from one pass, scores them all with the target in one tree pass, and verifies the best.",
 "7B drafters are too slow for 13-14B targets, diffusion drafting lacks KV caching and tuned kernels, and the analysis of its best-of-K acceptance rule is left open. Batch size is never reported.",
 "diffusion drafting")

add("c_2511_15898",
 "Solves optimal multi-draft verification: it shows the main formulations equal a relaxed optimal-transport LP and, via max-flow and polymatroid structure, reduces it to a convex problem in at most vocabulary-size variables, giving near-optimal acceptance for n i.i.d. drafts.",
 "Applies only to i.i.d. drafts from one drafter at a single step. The CPU solver can fail and takes up to 100 ms per token, and its tunable approximation leaves a small per-token deviation, so it is not exactly lossless.",
 "verification rule")

add("c_2511_17826",
 "Tree-Based Invariant Kernels: matmul and all-reduce follow one fixed binary-tree reduction order across intra- and inter-GPU levels, so results are bitwise identical for any tensor-parallel size from 1 to 8. Integrated into vLLM and FSDP.",
 "The fixed reduction order costs speed (the tree matmul reaches about 63% of cuBLAS BF16 throughput), quantized dtypes are unsupported, and only dense 7-32B models were tested.",
 "exact numerics")

add("sparsespec",
 "Self-speculation for long reasoning traces: the draft is the same model with sparse attention (PillarAttn) over tokens picked from attention scores already computed in the previous verification. A unified scheduler, delayed verification and dynamic KV management keep the GPU busy.",
 "Only attention is sparsified, so each draft token still reads all the weights. Gains rely on KV loading dominating; with short contexts, large batches make decoding compute-bound and the benefit fades.",
 "sparse self-speculation")

add("c_2512_23858",
 "Builds equal-growth trees with a fixed number of leaves per draft step, so shapes stay static for CUDA graphs and TorchInductor, while an MLP-predicted depth and greedy width maximize profiled end-to-end speedup, which accounts for verification latency. Adds DP width pruning and ahead-of-time draft scheduling.",
 "Assumes one interactive request owns the GPU, which does not carry over to batched serving. The depth predictor must be trained per dataset and model pair, and tests used only Llama-2 7B/13B with 68M/160M drafters.",
 "token trees")

add("c_2512_22420",
 "A contextual bandit keyed on current batch size picks the speculative length each step, including zero to switch SD off, and accounts for the KV-rebuild cost of switching. While SD is off under memory pressure, the draft model moves to CPU to free KV memory.",
 "Switching costs come from an offline-profiled, deployment-specific lookup table. It handles only chain drafts from small separate drafters, tested in vLLM on a single 4090/A100 plus one 2-GPU 32B run.",
 "serving under load")

add("c_2601_11580",
 "A systematic vLLM study of n-gram, EAGLE/EAGLE-3, draft-model and MTP speculation at batch 1-128: verification dominates step time, and acceptance varies within and across requests. Oracle simulations bound the gains from verifying only accepted tokens and from choosing the method per position.",
 "A measurement study at temperature 0 with mostly 3-token chains on H100. Its oracle bounds assume perfect acceptance prediction, so they show headroom without a method that reaches it.",
 "serving measurement")

add("dart",
 "A one-layer drafter on fused target features appends d-1 mask tokens and emits d next-token distributions in a single pass, removing serial drafting. It builds the draft tree by beam search over per-position top-k, scored by draft log-prob plus an n-gram continuity term.",
 "Its masked positions never see the tokens drafted before them, and its acceptance length (about 3.6-4.1) does not beat EAGLE-3's. Designed for a short horizon (d=8), and speedup decays to 1.45x at batch 64.",
 "parallel drafting")

add("srt",
 "Model-free speculative rollouts for RL: a per-prompt tree cache of earlier continuations serves as the draft. Trees are updated online from ongoing rollouts, and idle GPU bubbles run ahead on prompts due soon, so their cache is warm when they arrive.",
 "Drafts are verbatim copies of cached text, so acceptance depends on rollouts repeating. The workshop evaluation uses only Qwen2.5-1.5B, and the effects of online updates and run-ahead are shown in simulation.",
 "RL rollouts")

add("hsd",
 "A lossless sequence-level verifier: it scans the draft backward for the longest prefix acceptable under joint and capped-prefix probability ratios, then resamples once from a branch-level residual. This recovers the target distribution without intractable joint probabilities and plugs into multi-draft and EAGLE-3.",
 "Gains are modest (+3-12% block efficiency) in a batch-1 implementation. With EAGLE-3's deterministic top-k drafting the verification degenerates, so EAGLE-3H gains come mostly from implementation speed.",
 "verification rule")

add("c_2601_07353",
 "Grows EAGLE-3 trees layer by layer under a global node budget, keeping at each depth only candidates whose cumulative path probability is within a factor mu of that depth's best. Confident contexts get deep, narrow trees and uncertain ones shallow, wide trees.",
 "Evaluated only at batch size 1. At large batch the GPU saturates and per-request dynamic trees complicate memory management, and mu and the node budget may need retuning per setting.",
 "token trees")

add("c_2601_17768",
 "Makes decoding deterministic only for requests that ask: tokens are decoded fast with ordinary nondeterministic batching, then a fixed-shape verifier replays token windows, commits matching tokens and rolls back mismatches. Small windows from many requests are verified together.",
 "Replay is recomputation, so overhead grows with window size (6.8% at 32 tokens, 46% at 256). It lacks prefix-cache sharing, does not support speculative decoding, and was tested only on Llama-3.1-8B in SGLang.",
 "exact numerics")

input.message:
I wrote all 38 entries for batch1 to /tmp/diary/out1.json, one per key, each with intro, why_short and tag. Every paper was verified, so there are none I couldn't check.

- **Papers without catalogue text (14):** hetero, griffin, quantspec, longspec, multisample, adaspec, traversal, specextend, stand, logitspec, rhymerl, seer, sparsespec, srt. I read each one's arXiv abstract and full HTML text, including its limitations section where it had one, before writing.
- **The other 24:** I wrote these from their catalogue text and later_fixes.
- **Length:** each intro and why_short is at most 45 words, and each tag is 2 to 3 words.
- **Proposed entry:** this batch has no proposed=true paper, so it has no group-aware drafting entry.

**Limitations that come from the full papers, not from batch1.json:**
- **QuantSpec:** the target itself runs on an INT8 KV cache, so it is exact only relative to that model, not the FP16 one.
- **Traversal verification:** it is lossless only when the tree's children are sampled from the drafter, and it gives no gain at greedy decoding.
- **LongSpec:** the drafter's cross-attention only sees target KV up to the last verification, so later draft positions use stale context.
- **Seer:** group context adds only about 0.22 accepted tokens over a plain suffix tree.
- **RhymeRL:** it drafts only from earlier epochs' responses to the same prompt, never from sibling samples in the same step.

To fetch the papers I created two scratch directories under /tmp. I deleted both afterwards, so out1.json is the only file left from this run.
